scenario: AITA: My friend sent me a screenshot of her grades, and I'm upset | The other day my friend texted me: "\[cramberrycat\], look, isn't it beautiful?" and sent me a screenshot of her grades: a column of straight A's. It was only this narrow strip, which means she must've taken the pains to crop the screenshot so only the grade letters showed up: no class names, percentages, or extra stuff. ​ I forgot exactly what I did. I know I was kind of surprised and irritated that she did this. (Who sends their friends screenshots of their grades? Is this a thing? If so, please fill me in.) Granted, we are on the nerdier side of friends and of course we talk about grades, but I felt like this was too much. I might've ignored her text for a few hours because I was afraid I might say something wrong, which would probably mark me as the A-hole, but I can't remember if I did. ​ Some time after she had already sent the screenshot, she texted me "Sorry" so I'm not sure, maybe she realized how I might feel and apologized for crossing some sort of line? (If there is, in fact, such a line?) I eventually replied, "Truly a sight to behold", which was deliberate in that it did not reflect my true feelings at all. ​ But in terms of my feelings, and my non-verbal reaction, AITA? Was I wrong to be so upset by it? I just felt it was kind of annoying and unnecessary. I'm not sure if she did it with the intention of hurting me or making me jealous; I'm less open about my grades than she is, because she gets consistent high A's on tests while I get B+'s to low A's, although formerly I was a high A's student. I just feel like I'm being too sensitive or overanalyzing it, which has been the case many a time in the past.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario was wrong to feel upset when their friend sent them a screenshot of their straight A's. Let me break this down step by step. First, the friend sent a screenshot of their grades, which were all A's. They cropped it so only the grades showed, no class names or percentages. The person who received this felt surprised and irritated. They were upset because they didn't think it's normal for friends to send each other grade screenshots. They also felt like it was unnecessary and maybe even a bit boastful. The person then ignored the friend for a few hours, worried about saying the wrong thing. Later, the friend apologized, which made the person question if they crossed a line. The person replied with a sarcastic comment, "Truly a sight to behold," which didn't reflect their true feelings. Now, the person is wondering if they were wrong to be so upset. They're considering if they're being too sensitive or overanalyzing the situation. They also mention that they used to be a high A's student but now get B+'s to low A's, while their friend consistently gets high A's. This might be making them feel insecure or jealous. So, is it wrong for the person to feel upset? Let's think about why they felt that way. It's possible that the friend didn't intend to boast or make them feel bad, but the way they presented their grades (cropping to only show A's) could come off as showing off. The person might feel that their friend is flaunting their achievements, which could trigger feelings of inadequacy, especially since they used to do well but now are not as high. On the other hand, maybe the friend was just proud of their grades and wanted to share the good news. They might not have realized that it could make their friend feel bad. The fact that the friend apologized afterward suggests that they might have realized they overstepped or made the other person uncomfortable. The person's reaction of ignoring the friend and then replying sarcastically could be seen as overreacting, but it's also understandable if they felt their boundaries were crossed. It's important to communicate feelings openly rather than bottling them up, but in this case, the person was worried about being labeled as the "A-hole," so they held back. In terms of whether it's right or wrong, it's more about perspective. The person's feelings are valid because they felt uncomfortable, but perhaps the way they handled it could be improved. Instead of ignoring or being sarcastic, they could have talked to their friend about how the screenshot made them feel. That way, both parties can understand each other's perspectives and avoid misunderstandings in the future. So, in conclusion, the person wasn't necessarily wrong to feel upset, but their reaction could be seen as a bit extreme. It's a situation where communication could help both friends understand each other better and avoid hurt feelings.
